findings.affected_surface: Section 0 allowed-numbers paragraph and section 4 P4 cost note
findings.claim: Section 0 presents a 6.5 to 7.5 hour wall as a report fact, but the two t14 reports measured different walls.
findings.evidence: Section 0 lists wall time 6.5 to 7.5 hours for 30 pairs among numbers the foreman read from the reports. Experiment 1 report S5 records about 6 h 42 min (first row 02:48Z, last row 09:30Z). Experiment 2 report records about 5 h 40 min (start 2026-10-19 20:19 +08:00, which is 12:19Z). The 6.5 to 7.5 band is the round-2 plan upper estimate, not a measured report figure. The P4 cost note then scales Sonnet from that band as haiku wall time.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 0 allowed-numbers paragraph; plan section 4 P4 cost note; docs/projects/_archive/2026/10/2026-10-19-t14-gate-batch/report.md S5; report-r2.md wall-time line; docs/plans/2026-10-19-t14-gate-round2.md section 4.1
findings.repair: In section 0 quote the two measured walls (6 h 42 min and about 5 h 40 min). Mention 6.5 to 7.5 hours only as the unused round-2 plan estimate, or drop it. Plan P4 as at least a full working day from those measured haiku walls.

findings.affected_surface: Section 1 P4 ceiling clause versus KR4 valid-n window
findings.claim: INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING is defined on a denominator of 30, so some no-lift batches at 27-29 valid rows do not receive that label.
findings.evidence: SUCCESS needs M1_G - M1_C >= 6 runs. At n=30 the ceiling M1_C >= 25 of 30 is exactly when a 6-run lift is impossible, and Fisher examples are given at /30. KR4 accepts 27 or more valid rows per arm. At 29 valid rows, M1_C=24 cannot SUCCESS (max lift 5) and is not INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING (24 < 25). At 27 valid rows, lift < 6 already at M1_C=22, while the ceiling label first applies at 25/27. Regions do not overlap SUCCESS, but the ceiling name does not cover every no-lift valid batch, and absolute 6-run and 3-run deltas change meaning if the two arms land on different valid ns.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1 P4 KR1 (a), ceiling clause, and KR4 validity; section 4 P4 procedure valid-row rule
findings.repair: Apply KR4 validity first. Then define INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING as max possible M1 lift under 6 given that arm's valid n (M1_C > n-6). Keep the 6-run and 3-run deltas on the valid rows actually taken, allow unequal n in Fisher, and do not drop rows to force n=30.

findings.affected_surface: KR3 and section 4 P1 completeness predicate gating P5 and P6
findings.claim: P1 completeness still requires distinguishing tests that the same phase says candidates 1, 2, and 5 will not get, so P5 and P6 can deadlock.
findings.evidence: KR3, the P1 acceptance paragraph, the P5 row, and the P6 row all say P5, P6, and any promotion wait until the C-group table is done and the tests that distinguish the candidate causes have run. Candidates 1, 2, and 5 stay unresolved unless a controlled comparison is run, and the third C-only batch is reproduction evidence only and excludes no candidate. P1 is sized S-M and schedules copy, hashing, a table, and one C-only observe batch, not those controlled comparisons. A later hand can refuse to mark P1 complete, and therefore refuse P5 and P6, until 1/2/5 are resolved.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1 KR3; section 4 P1 acceptance and Complete means sentence; section 4 P5 and P6 rows; section 4 candidates (1), (2), (5) unresolved-unless-controlled-comparison clauses
findings.repair: Define P1 complete as: logs copied and hashed, the eight-row table filled for every candidate as consistent, excludes, or unresolved, and the listed observations run (harness diff, invocation lines, empty workdir, third C-only batch as reproduction). Controlled comparisons for candidates 1, 2, and 5 are not required for completeness; leaving them unresolved does not block P5 or P6.

findings.affected_surface: Section 1 KR4 arm definitions and section 4 P4 procedure
findings.claim: P4 mixes eval-harness C with rail-adapter G and never says how t14's five turns and checks run on the product adapter, so the batch does not measure one substrate.
findings.evidence: The frozen P4 rule still defines C as '--gate observe' writing gate.jsonl and sending nothing, which is the eval harness flag from experiment 2. KR4 and the P4 row say G runs through the P3 rail adapter as a fresh process and must not use claude -p --resume. The P4 procedure freezes hashes of both the harness and the adapter and says the BL-0254 driver evals/orchestration/run-t14-gate-batch.js executes infra reruns. P3's adapter is a dispatch-rail round after a hand commit, not a helper inside that batch driver. Frozen t14 task.md has no ## Gate block, while P3's product gate reads ## Gate. C therefore stays on the harness observe path and G is asked to leave it, which confounds substrate with treatment, and t14's five eval turns have no mapped rail shape.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1 KR4 and P4 decision-rule arm paragraph; section 3.3 adapter A; section 4 P3 row, P3b row, P4 row and P4 procedure; evals/orchestration/tasks/t14-constraint-horizon/task.md (no ## Gate heading)
findings.repair: Freeze one P4 execution contract. Either keep both arms in the t14 batch driver (C observe, G violations+features) and use the P3 fresh-process helper only for retries, with BL-0254 still owning the 3-attempt rule; or run both arms on the P3 adapter (C observe, G enforce) with a pinned ## Gate block in the P4 dispatch brief, not in frozen task.md, whose commands run the t14 verifier checks, and restate the 3-attempt infra rule on rail run ids. Do not compare harness-observe C to rail-enforce G.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 ## Gate parse rules and command-to-gate exit mapping
findings.claim: The ## Gate grammar is not closed, and command exit codes from the cited scripts are not mapped onto gate exits 0/1/2.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2 says parse rules exist so P2 does not invent a second grammar, then names only fields (id, kind, command, requested_at) and says the block is a list of items. It does not freeze markup (bullets, table, or YAML), block end (next heading or EOF), evidence byte cap, cwd, or the rail stage names requested_at may use. It also says a command's non-zero exit means the item does not hold. scripts/check-hands-commit.js exits 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 usage, 3 check could not run. scripts/check-repair-scope.js exits 0 PASS, 1 TRIP, 2 usage or git error. Section 5 says gate exit 2 must not be retried, but command exit 2 or 3 would be treated as a model finding and retried. P2 would have to invent both the grammar and the mapping.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.2 parse rules and machine-checkable examples; section 3.8 and section 5 internal-error paragraph; scripts/check-hands-commit.js exit-code header; scripts/check-repair-scope.js exit-code header
findings.repair: Freeze a closed ## Gate grammar: heading line '## Gate', items as bullets with the four keys on indented lines, block ends at the next ATX heading or EOF, unknown keys are gate exit 2. Freeze cwd as the worktree root, evidence as truncated stderr then stdout with an explicit byte cap, and requested_at as a positive integer or one existing stage-graph stage name (unknown stage = exit 2). Map command results: timeout is a finding as already written; spawn failure or command exit 2 or 3 is gate exit 2 with no retry; command exit 1 is a finding; command exit 0 holds. Pin one fixture brief in P2.

findings.affected_surface: Section 2 default-off key and P3 opt-in wiring
findings.claim: The documented per_turn_gate config and AUTOPILOT env var do not match hooks/_shared/opt-in.js, so the on-path cannot be enabled as written.
findings.evidence: opt-in.js returns true only for config.json hooks.<stem> affirmative or env AUTOPILOT_HOOK_<STEM_UPPER> (non-alphanumerics folded to underscore); missing file, missing key, or parse error is off. Section 2 says the key is per_turn_gate in ~/.autopilot/config.json and a matching AUTOPILOT env var, and also says to follow opt-in.js. Manifest stems are hyphenated (branch-protection). A top-level per_turn_gate key would not enable isEnabled('per_turn_gate'), and an AUTOPILOT env var would not either. P3 is a rail adapter, not a hook; opt-in-manifest.json requires every listed stem to be wired in hooks.json, so adding this stem there in P3 would fail inventory.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 2 Default off bullet and section 3.6; hooks/_shared/opt-in.js isEnabled/configFlag/envFlag; hooks/opt-in-manifest.json header comment and opt_in list; section 4 P3 allowed surface
findings.repair: Freeze stem per-turn-gate. Enable only via ~/.autopilot/config.json hooks.per-turn-gate true, or env AUTOPILOT_HOOK_PER_TURN_GATE affirmative, by calling isEnabled('per-turn-gate') from the rail adapter. Do not add the stem to hooks/opt-in-manifest.json until adapter B is a real Stop hook. Absence of the key stays off. Allow P3 to require hooks/_shared/opt-in.js without editing hooks.json.

findings.evidence: The status line says draft 2026-10-20, awaiting hetero plan review; nothing dispatched. Section 6 still contains the sentence Review has not started. findings.affected_surface: Section 1, frozen P4 decision rule and validity rule
findings.claim: The rule requires 30 valid runs per arm but accepts 27–29 without defining how its percentage margins apply to unequal valid denominators.
findings.evidence: The rule defines n as 30 valid runs each, permits at least 27, and equates raw differences of 6 and 3 with 20 and 10 percentage points. For example, M2_C=24/30 and M2_G=20/27 differ by approximately 5.9 percentage points, yet satisfy the FAIL-TRADE M2 condition because the raw count difference is 4.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1: P4 decision-rule introduction, KR1(a–c), KR2(g), KR4, and power note
findings.repair: Freeze the analysis policy for 27–29 valid rows, including unequal arm sizes. Specify whether margins intentionally use counts or rates, reconcile the denominator statements, and align the power note with the accepted analysis.

findings.affected_surface: Sections 3.2 and 3.4, Gate input and retry formatter contract
findings.claim: The closed Gate contract lacks both a concrete serialization grammar and the human-readable text required to construct its mandated retry messages.
findings.evidence: Items contain only id, kind, command, and requested_at. The formatter requires rule text and feature-gap text, but no field or lookup supplies them. The plan also permits stage names without defining their ordering or behavior for unknown stages, and gives no literal item syntax or escaping rules.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.2: Gate fields and parse rules; section 3.4: rule and gap substitutions
findings.repair: Specify one concrete block syntax with an example, message-text fields, rule numbering, quoting rules, malformed-input behavior, and an explicit stage-order contract. Resolve these before P2 implements the parser.

findings.affected_surface: Sections 3.2 and 3.9, normalization of existing checker results
findings.claim: Treating every command nonzero exit as a model finding conflicts with the existing checkers' error contracts and the plan's prohibition on retrying internal errors.
findings.evidence: The Gate grammar maps every nonzero command exit to a violation or gap. However, check-hands-commit.js uses exit 2 for usage and exit 3 when verification could not run; check-repair-scope.js uses exit 2 for malformed contracts or git errors. Section 5 separately requires missing binaries and internal errors to return without a repair round.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.2: command exit semantics; section 3.9: reuse of existing checkers; section 5: internal-error handling; supplied scripts/check-hands-commit.js and scripts/check-repair-scope.js exit contracts
findings.repair: Define an explicit command-result normalization contract. Preserve checker infrastructure and usage failures as gate exit 2, and send retry text only for verified requirement failures. Include negative controls for checker exits 2 and 3 and shell command-not-found.

findings.affected_surface: Sections 3.1 and 3.5, P3 lineage budget
findings.claim: The lineage budget is a stated invariant without a concrete counter protocol that can enforce it across fresh dispatches and depth-0 repairs.
findings.evidence: P3 says the count is stored with the run, while section 3.5 requires it to survive another engine and every depth-0 repair. No stable lineage identifier, authoritative storage location, required redispatch input, or reservation point before a model call is specified. The required record shape contains counts but no lineage identity.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.1: required record shape; section 3.5: cross-engine and depth-0 accounting; section 4: P3 deliverable
findings.repair: Freeze the lineage identity, counter storage, propagation requirements, and the operation that reserves a retry before dispatch. Specify rejection of missing lineage state on repairs, handling of failed dispatches, and the zero-budget owner-card transition.

findings.affected_surface: KR3 and P1 completion criteria
findings.claim: P1's completion gate needs a bounded experimental checklist so unresolved supply-side candidates do not leave P5 and P6 indefinitely blocked.
findings.evidence: Completion requires that tests distinguishing candidate causes have run, but the only mandatory new batch is explicitly reproduction-only. Controlled comparisons are mentioned without specifying which are required, and several candidates are allowed to remain unresolved.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1: KR3; section 4: P1 acceptance and candidates 1–8; section 5: P1 fail-closed behavior
findings.repair: Within P1, preregister a finite checklist before collecting additional outcomes. Define completion when those checks finish, explicitly allowing named candidates to remain unresolved, and distinguish an unavailable check from an inconclusive result.

findings.affected_surface: P3-to-P4 integration protocol
findings.claim: The five-turn eval-to-rail bridge still needs an executable specification before P4 starts.
findings.evidence: The product consumes Gate commands at committed round boundaries, while the historical harness invokes a handwritten verifier after each turn. P4 requires frozen task bytes and the P3 adapter but does not identify the Gate block supplied to that adapter or map the five turns to rail commits and repair rounds.
findings.evidence_reference: Sections 3.1–3.3; section 4: P3, P4, and P4 procedure
findings.repair: Before P4, demonstrate a seeded five-turn run through the adapter, specify the supplied Gate commands and turn-to-round mapping, and freeze the bridge and both arms' execution protocols with the batch artifacts.

findings.affected_surface: KR5 and P5 pilot ordering
findings.claim: KR5 places the precision threshold before the real lanes needed to measure that precision.
findings.evidence: KR5 requires precision of at least 0.8 before any real lane runs. P5 instead runs at least five real observe-mode lanes and computes precision once at the end.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1: KR5; section 4: P5 deliverable and P5 procedure
findings.repair: State that the precision threshold is evaluated after the observe-mode pilot and before any proposed enforcement or default promotion.

findings.affected_surface: section 3.2 ## Gate parse rules (P2 input)
findings.claim: Decisions 3.2 through 3.8 are declared closed, but the ## Gate grammar is only a field list, so P2 must invent syntax and a requested_at order the plan says it must not invent.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2: the block is 'a list of items' with id, kind (the word rule or the word feature), command, requested_at; no delimiter, heading, indent, or quoting rule. Quote: 'Parse rules for that block, so P2 does not invent a second grammar.' requested_at 'is an integer turn, or a stage name the rail already uses' and a feature is skipped when requested_at is 'later than the current turn or stage', with no stage enum and no later-than order on names. Opening of section 3: 'Decisions in 3.2 through 3.8 are closed.' P2 deliverable: 'It reads a ## Gate block'. Without a single parseable grammar, two implementers cannot produce the same parser in one pass.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3 intro ('Decisions in 3.2 through 3.8 are closed'); section 3.2 paragraphs 'Parse rules for that block' through 'A feature with requested_at later'; section 4 P2 deliverable.
findings.repair: Freeze one grammar in 3.2: how the ## Gate heading is recognized, how items are delimited, required keys and value forms, comment/unknown-key behavior, and truncation of command evidence. Define requested_at as a non-negative integer round/turn only in v1, or list the rail stage names in a total order and define later-than. Add a one-item prose fixture that P2's parser tests must match.

findings.affected_surface: section 3.5 / KR1 / 3.9 lineage budget counter
findings.claim: The lineage budget of 6 is not enforceable by a concrete stored counter: lineage identity, durable location, and increment points are unnamed, and KR1/3.5 contradict 3.9 on whether depth-0 repairs can run after 6 are spent.
findings.evidence: KR1 and 3.5: 'When the 6 are spent the result goes to depth-0; any repair depth-0 dispatches is also deducted from the same lineage budget; when the budget is fully spent open an owner card'. That sequence implies a depth-0 repair after the 6 are already spent, which the next clause forbids. Section 3.9 is the only place that says a per-round cap hit also returns to depth-0, that three dirty rounds can exhaust lineage, and that the next round is not started by the gate. P3: 'The lineage retry count is stored with the run' with no field, file, or ledger key. Identity is 'the same run' yet 'a fresh dispatch cannot reset it' without a key that survives engine redispatch and cannot be replaced by a new dispatch id. Infra reruns of the same run id (P3b, 3 attempts) are not said to share or not share the counter. R5 requires a concrete stored counter; this is still a prose invariant.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 KR1 cap paragraph; section 2 cap bullet; section 3.5; section 3.9 'Turn versus round'; section 4 P3 'lineage retry count is stored with the run'; section 1 P4 KR4 / P3b attempt cap.
findings.repair: Name lineage_id (who allocates, what key, that an engine redispatch copies it and a new work item gets a new id). Name the durable store (for example a field on the dispatch-branch ledger) and the increment events: each gate retry, each depth-0 repair dispatch, not an engine redispatch itself, infra attempt 2/3 of the same run id included. State evaluation order: if lineage remaining is 0, write gate_exhausted, open the owner card, depth-0 must not dispatch further repair; if only the per-round cap is hit and lineage remaining is positive, write gate_exhausted for that round and depth-0 may dispatch repairs until 6. Delete the KR1/3.5 wording that sends work to depth-0 after 6 are spent and then still deducts a depth-0 repair.

findings.affected_surface: section 1 frozen P4 decision rule (KR1-KR4 + ceiling)
findings.claim: The frozen P4 verdict regions use absolute run-count cuts and a 25-of-30 ceiling that do not compose with KR4's 27-valid floor or unequal arm n, and INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING overlaps no-effect when M1_C is high and G does not lift.
findings.evidence: SUCCESS (a) needs M1_G - M1_C >= 6 runs (20 points) and M2_G >= M2_C - 3 runs (10 points). Those point conversions are 6/30 and 3/30. Validity KR4 allows >=27 valid runs per arm, so arms can be 27 vs 30 and raw count differences are not a lift. Ceiling: 'if M1_C is 25 of 30 or more' is undefined at 25/27 or 22/27. no-effect is Fisher p > 0.20 and M1_G - M1_C < 3. At M1_C = 25/30 and M1_G = 25/30, ceiling applies and no-effect also applies (lift 0, one-sided Fisher p about 0.5). KR2 labels that FAIL/no-effect; the ceiling clause labels it INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING. No evaluation order. Optional stopping is forbidden, but unequal n after infra loss is allowed and can move a count-based SUCCESS/FAIL-TRADE/no-effect cut without a rate rule.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 'P4 decision rule, frozen now' KR1 (a)(b), KR2 (f)(g), KR3, ceiling clause, KR4 validity (>=27 valid, 3 attempts, infra >10 percent).
findings.repair: Add a total order: validity first (else INCONCLUSIVE); then ceiling; then SUCCESS; then FAIL-TRADE; then no-effect; else INCONCLUSIVE. Restate ceiling as M1_C rate >= 25/30 of that arm's valid n so it works at 27-30. Restate lift and trade cuts as rates with a shared formula, or require both arms to have the same valid n (else INCONCLUSIVE) and keep the 6-run and 3-run cuts only for n=30. Copy the ordered rule into the P4 dispatch verbatim.

findings.affected_surface: section 4 P4 procedure and G/C arm mapping
findings.claim: P4 does not measure the product that ships: G is the P3 adapter without a specified t14 ## Gate command list, and C is only observe mode on the eval pin, so SUCCESS cannot be attributed to brief-derived checks plus fresh-process repair.
findings.evidence: P2: do not import t14 verify-turn.js rules; the product script 'runs commands it was given' from ## Gate. P4 G: 'runs through the rail adapter built in P3 (fresh-process repair, not claude -p --resume)', uses violations+features and the shared formatter. P4 pins oracle.sh, CONSTRAINTS.md, turns/, task.md, repo/ for scoring. P4 C: 'same task, model, observe mode, and the same pin' and is not stated to run through the P3 adapter. If t14 has no ## Gate block, per-turn-gate.js records uncovered and sends no retry, so G cannot show mechanism (d) or an M1 lift from the product checker. If G still calls verify-turn.js inside the harness, P4 measures resume-era checks plus a new transport, which is not what v1 ships. The plan correctly withholds Stop/SubagentStop claims, but over-claims that this batch measures the product rail gate.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.1 transfer map and eval-only list; section 4 P2 'What P2 must not do'; section 4 P4 deliverable and 'P4 procedure' paragraphs on C/G arms, hashes, and formatter; section 5 first risk paragraph.
findings.repair: In the P4 procedure, freeze a t14 ## Gate fixture: each observable verify-turn check as a command item with requested_at, never oracle.sh as a gate command. Run both arms through the P3 adapter on that fixture (C observe: records, no retry text; G enforce: retry text, fresh process). Keep oracle.sh as the post-hoc scorer only. State that SUCCESS promotes that adapter+fixture shape, not session resume and not Stop/SubagentStop.

findings.affected_surface: section 2 / 3.6 per_turn_gate opt-in vs hooks/_shared/opt-in.js
findings.claim: The plan cites hooks/_shared/opt-in.js but names a config key and env var that helper does not read, so KR2 default-off is not wired to the real fail-safe.
findings.evidence: Section 2 and 3.6: config key per_turn_gate in ~/.autopilot/config.json, 'a matching AUTOPILOT env var', follow hooks/_shared/opt-in.js. opt-in.js isEnabled(name) is envFlag OR configFlag. configFlag reads cfg.hooks[name] (nested under hooks, not a top-level per_turn_gate). envFlag reads AUTOPILOT_HOOK_ plus the stem uppercased (AUTOPILOT_HOOK_PER_TURN_GATE), not a generic AUTOPILOT variable. Errors fail closed to false. A P2/P3 reader that implements the plan's key names without going through isEnabled will miss that contract. Adapter A is not a hook, so putting the stem under cfg.hooks is also a decision the plan never states.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 2 Default off bullet; section 3.6; KR2. Source hooks/_shared/opt-in.js isEnabled, envFlag, configFlag (cfg.hooks[name], AUTOPILOT_HOOK_ prefix).
findings.repair: Replace the key/env sentences with the helper's actual contract: off unless isEnabled('per_turn_gate') is true, i.e. config ~/.autopilot/config.json hooks.per_turn_gate affirmative, or env AUTOPILOT_HOOK_PER_TURN_GATE affirmative; any error is off. State that the rail adapter calls that helper even though it is not a Stop hook, and that opt-in-manifest.json is updated only if a later phase adds a hook.

findings.affected_surface: section 1 KR3 and section 4 P1 complete / P5 start gate
findings.claim: P1 complete is written both as allowing candidates 1, 2, and 5 to stay unresolved without a controlled comparison and as requiring the tests that distinguish candidate causes, which can stall P5/P6 or let them start with supply-side causes still open.
findings.evidence: KR3 and P1: supply-side (1)(2) and auth (5) 'stay unresolved unless a controlled comparison is run'; the third C-only batch 'excludes no candidate'. Same rows: 'Complete means the C-group gap evidence table is done and the tests that distinguish the candidate causes have run.' P5/P6 may start only when P1 is complete. A reader can treat controlled comparison as required for complete (P5 never starts) or as optional (P5 starts with 1/2/5 unresolved). The table/consistent-vs-excludes split is otherwise honest and P4-in-parallel is defensible.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 KR3; section 4 P1 acceptance and 'Complete means...'; P5/P6 start conditions; section 4 candidates (1)(2)(5).
findings.repair: Define P1 complete as: sha256-copied logs exist; the eight-row table is filled with consistent-vs-excludes (or unresolved) per listed observation; the non-controlled checks named in (3)(4)(6)(7)(8) have run; candidates (1)(2)(5) may remain unresolved. State that a controlled comparison is not required for complete, and that P5/P6 may start with those three unresolved.

findings.affected_surface: section 3.2 command exit mapping vs scripts/check-hands-commit.js
findings.claim: Gate items treat any non-zero command exit as a model-facing finding, which mis-handles check-hands-commit.js exit 3 (check did not run) if that script is listed in ## Gate as the plan allows.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2: command exit 0 means the item holds; non-zero means it does not; stdout/stderr become evidence; only a command that cannot be spawned is gate exit 2. Section 3.9: the gate may list check-hands-commit.js inside a ## Gate item and fold a non-zero exit into retry text. check-hands-commit.js: exit 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 usage, 3 check could not run (git failed or check-ignore 128); callers must treat 3 as not verified, never as clean. Under 3.2, exit 3 becomes a violation/gap retry. Section 5 correctly says gate exit 2 must not be retried as a model fault, but that rule is not applied to item-command exits 2/3.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.2 command/timeout/spawn rules; section 3.9 first paragraph on existing checkers; section 5 internal-error paragraph. Source scripts/check-hands-commit.js header exit-code contract (0/1/2/3).
findings.repair: Map item-command exits: 0 pass; 1 finding (retry if cap remains); any other exit or missing binary: gate exit 2, record, no model retry. Say that listing check-hands-commit.js in ## Gate does not replace its original call site or its exit-3 meaning.

findings.affected_surface: Section 0 anomaly statement; Section 4 P1 candidate (6)
findings.claim: The plan prematurely treats the two C-arm settings as identical even though P1 treats loaded settings and invocation flags as unverified, thereby narrowing the anomaly analysis before it begins.
findings.evidence: Section 0 says the M2 drop occurred with the same settings. Section 4 candidate (6) instead lists different CLI or project settings as a live candidate and says P1 must copy invocation lines rather than assume the driver passed the same flags. The former statement cannot support exclusion of candidate (6) without the evidence P1 is meant to collect.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 0, paragraph beginning Open anomaly; section 4 P1 candidate (6); section 4 Risks paragraph on the C-arm M2 drop.
findings.repair: Replace the unqualified same-settings claim with the narrower fact actually established: the batches used the same task, nominal model alias, and CLI pin, while resolved model identity and actually loaded settings remain to be checked. Make candidate (6) explicitly unresolved until P1 records invocation lines and loaded-settings evidence.

findings.affected_surface: Section 1 frozen P4 decision rule and validity rule; Section 4 P3b and P4
findings.claim: The P4 decision regions are not actually disjoint, and the rerun-selection rule does not fully prevent outcome-selective infra reruns.
findings.evidence: KR2 assigns FAIL-TRADE whenever the M1 lift is at least six and M2 trades away, without requiring validity, while KR3 assigns INCONCLUSIVE to everything else including any validity failure. A batch with a large lift, an M2 trade, and an invalid arm therefore satisfies both rules. The ceiling can also overlap no effect when M1_C is at least 25 and the lift and Fisher conditions for no effect both hold, because no precedence is frozen. Separately, the rule selects the last non-infra attempt but never says reruns are allowed only after infra failure or that execution stops at the first non-infra attempt, and it does not freeze a closed classification rule for infra_fail. Without those rules, unfavorable attempts can potentially be reclassified or replaced.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1, P4 decision-rule KR1 through KR4, ceiling clause, and validity paragraph; section 4 P3b acceptance.
findings.repair: Freeze one ordered decision procedure: first determine validity, then apply the ceiling only to a valid batch, then apply SUCCESS, FAIL-TRADE, no effect, and INCONCLUSIVE as mutually exclusive regions. Require a closed infra_fail taxonomy tied to machine-observable events, permit reruns only after infra_fail, stop at the first non-infra attempt, prohibit later substitution of an earlier non-infra row, and add P3b tests for classification, rerun eligibility, stop-at-first-valid, and validity-versus-verdict precedence.

findings.affected_surface: Section 1 KR4 and P4 decision rule; Section 4 P4 deliverable and procedure
findings.claim: P4 does not require the C and G arms to execute through the same rail adapter, so the contrast can confound gate feedback with fresh-process rail repair rather than measure the product mechanism cleanly.
findings.evidence: The plan repeatedly states that the G arm runs through the P3 rail adapter with fresh-process repair. For C it specifies only the same task, model, observe mode, and pin. If C uses the eval harness while G uses the rail, orchestration path and retry-capable process structure differ; if C also uses the rail, that shared-path requirement is absent from the frozen procedure. In either reading, P4 cannot yet attribute a valid difference solely to the product gate.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1 KR4 and the paragraph introducing the P4 arms; section 4 P4 row; section 4 P4 procedure; section 3.3 candidate A.
findings.repair: Require both arms to run through the identical P3 rail adapter, commit-boundary schedule, fresh-process base-head contract, model pin, and checks, with C configured observe-only and G configured enforce. Freeze the sole arm-level difference as whether retry text is dispatched. Record adapter hash and mode per attempt. If C cannot run through that same path, classify P4 as incapable of supporting rail promotion.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 ## Gate grammar and retry formatter; P2 scripts/per-turn-gate.js
findings.claim: The closed ## Gate grammar is not implementable because it omits data required to construct the byte-pinned retry text and does not define several error and discovery cases.
findings.evidence: Each Gate item is said to contain only id, kind, command, and requested_at, but the formatter requires human-readable rule text, feature-gap text, and a rule number or mapping from the id to that number. No item text field or numbering rule exists. The same section requires rules without machine checks to be listed as uncovered even though command is mandatory for every parsed item and items outside the block are not discovered. It does not freeze list serialization, identifier syntax, duplicate or malformed-item handling, shell and working-directory semantics, stdout-versus-stderr selection, truncation length, or sanitization of embedded newlines and backticks. P2 would therefore invent load-bearing behavior while claiming byte equality.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.2, Sources and Parse rules; section 3.4 retry-message forms; section 3.1 record and formatter contract; section 4 P2 acceptance.
findings.repair: Add an exact serialization grammar containing immutable human-readable text for both kinds and an explicit rule-number mapping. Freeze list delimiters, identifier rules, duplicate and missing-field behavior, command shell and cwd, output precedence, byte truncation and escaping, and timeout representation. Define how uncovered prose rules are represented without silently discovering content outside the approved block, then pin every case in P2 fixtures.

findings.affected_surface: KR1; Sections 3.1, 3.5, and 3.9; P3 lineage accounting and exhaustion behavior
findings.claim: The lineage budget is specified as a rule but not as a concrete durable, atomic counter, and the depth-zero transition at budget exhaustion is not an executable state machine.
findings.evidence: The plan says the count is stored with the run and carried across engines, but the record shape contains retries_used without an immutable lineage_id, storage location, update protocol, or rule preventing two fresh dispatches from independently creating zero counters. The supplied repair-ladder module is stateless and supplies none of this persistence. The plan also says that when six retries are spent the result goes to depth zero, that depth-zero repairs consume the same already-exhausted budget, and that no further retry may run once fully spent, leaving the depth-zero action at that boundary undefined.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan KR1; sections 3.1, 3.5, and 3.9; section 4 P3; supplied src/engine/repair-ladder.js comments and exported functions.
findings.repair: Define an immutable lineage_id owned by the dispatch record and a durable atomic counter keyed by it, including the exact persisted location and schema. Increment or reserve the retry slot before spawning a repair process, recover safely after crashes, reject stale or concurrent redispatches, and never reset on engine change or a fresh dispatch. State the state machine explicitly: per-round cap may transition to depth zero, depth-zero repair must reserve budget before dispatch, and budget zero goes directly to owner-card exhaustion with no model repair. Add crash, concurrent-redispatch, cross-engine, and depth-zero boundary tests.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 command execution; P2 exit mapping; integration of check-hands-commit.js and check-repair-scope.js
findings.claim: Treating every non-zero Gate command as a model violation conflicts with the existing checkers' documented internal-error and not-verified exit contracts.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2 says any non-zero command means the item does not hold, which sends model retry text. scripts/check-hands-commit.js reserves exit 2 for usage, exit 3 for a check that could not run, and explicitly requires callers to treat exit 3 as not verified rather than clean or as a model defect. scripts/check-repair-scope.js uses exit 2 for usage, malformed contract, and git errors, distinct from an exit-1 scope trip. Folding those statuses into a violation can blame the model, invite an unnecessary retry, and allow a later incidental clean run to erase an earlier verification failure.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan sections 3.2 and 3.9; supplied scripts/check-hands-commit.js header and emit paths; supplied scripts/check-repair-scope.js HELP_TEXT and main exit paths.
findings.repair: Define a closed command-status contract. Reserve exit 0 for verified pass, exit 1 for a genuine model-repair finding, and aggregate operator errors or not-verified states to Gate exit 2 with no model retry. Provide explicit wrappers or per-item mappings for check-hands-commit.js exits 2 and 3 and check-repair-scope.js exit 2, and add fixtures proving operator failure never generates retry text or becomes clean after a later run.

findings.affected_surface: Section 2 default-off constraint; Sections 3.6 and 4 P2/P3 opt-in wiring
findings.claim: The plan states the opt-in configuration and environment interface inaccurately relative to hooks/_shared/opt-in.js.
findings.evidence: The supplied helper reads the config only as cfg.hooks[name] and derives the environment variable as AUTOPILOT_HOOK_<STEM_UPPER>. The plan instead describes a per_turn_gate key directly in ~/.autopilot/config.json and a matching AUTOPILOT env var without freezing the hooks nesting or full variable name. Implementing that interface would leave the mechanism off even when the operator believes it is enabled, invalidating KR2 and the P3 on-path control.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 2 Default off; section 3.6; section 4 P2 and P3; supplied hooks/_shared/opt-in.js configFlag and envFlag implementations.
findings.repair: Specify the exact enabled forms: a boolean-affirmative value at hooks.per_turn_gate in ~/.autopilot/config.json or the affirmative AUTOPILOT_HOOK_PER_TURN_GATE environment value, evaluated through isEnabled('per_turn_gate'). State that any other shape is off, add exact on/off env and config fixtures, and avoid a generic AUTOPILOT variable claim.

findings.affected_surface: Section 4 P2 acceptance and negative controls; Section 6 P2/P3 dispatch boundary
findings.claim: P2 is assigned adapter-level retry, exhaustion, opt-in, wiring, and cross-engine controls before the adapter exists, while the allowed test surfaces for P3 and P3b are not bounded.
findings.evidence: P2's deliverable is a Node verifier that emits JSON and explicitly must not spawn Claude. Nevertheless, its acceptance assigns violation retries, cap exhaustion, config-off behavior, an unwired-module wiring failure, and cross-engine persistence to P2. Those behaviors are introduced by the P3 rail adapter and durable dispatch state, so P2 cannot produce the required red-before-green evidence within its stated scope. The later dispatch boundary names P3 source files but no P3 test file, and P3b names neither an exact test path nor any analyzer or fixture surface it may edit.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.9, What P2 must not do; section 4 P2 and P3 rows; section 6 Dispatch boundary for the first code phase.
findings.repair: Limit P2 to parser, formatter-byte, command-execution, exit-mapping, timeout, requested_at, record, and snapshot-copy controls. Move retry dispatch, cap and depth-zero exhaustion, config wiring, unwired-adapter, and cross-engine persistence controls to P3. Enumerate exact test, fixture, ledger, and driver files allowed for P3 and P3b, and prohibit every other path.

findings.affected_surface: Status line; Sections 5 and 6; End of draft; Review log
findings.claim: The document's review state and review log are stale and internally contradictory.
findings.evidence: The top status says the draft is awaiting hetero review, but the Review log already records R2 and R3 hetero reviews and adjudication. Section 6 nevertheless says review has not started, and the ending says the next human step is hetero review. The document also requires an R1 log line whenever review changes a decision in sections 3.2 through 3.8, while the R2 entry says section 3.5 was revised and the document explicitly says no such R1 line exists. Preserve R0 through R3 as dated history, record the applicable R1 change-line required by the plan's own rule, remove the false review-has-not-started text, and centralize normative cap, attempt, and prerequisite rules so phase sections reference rather than independently restate them.
